blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Logistics KPIs at board level serve a different purpose from operational ones. The board is not chasing a specific shipment or debating a picker's accuracy; it is trying to understand whether the logistics function is healthy enough to support the company's strategy over the next two or three years. That means the dashboard shows direction, risk and capability — not daily detail.

The right board dashboard has six or seven numbers, not thirty: service level trend by quarter, cost per unit trend, concentration of volume by carrier and by region, an honest read of exceptions and how they were resolved, and a simple risk rating against the biggest known scenarios. That is enough for a director to hold an intelligent conversation about logistics without becoming an operations expert.

The most common mistake is to paste the operational dashboard straight into the board pack. The right instinct is translation: take the real story of the function and tell it in the language the board can act on. Done well, this changes how the board sees logistics — from a cost centre to a source of strategic capability.

items.q: According to the text, what is the board trying to understand through logistics KPIs?
options: Whether the function can support strategy over the next few years
The status of a specific shipment
The daily detail of every warehouse
The accuracy of an individual picker
items.why: "whether the logistics function is healthy enough to support the company's strategy over the next two or three years."

items.q: How many numbers, ideally, does a good board dashboard contain?
options: As many as the operational dashboard
items.why: "The right board dashboard has six or seven numbers, not thirty."

items.q: What does the author call the most common mistake?
options: Leaving out the cost per unit trend
Showing a risk rating to directors
Pasting the operational dashboard straight into the board pack
items.why: "The most common mistake is to paste the operational dashboard straight into the board pack."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The more operational detail a director sees, the better the board decision.
Exceptions deserve an honest read at board level.
Logistics can be a source of strategic capability.
A board pack should speak in the language the board can act on.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta a favor de tradução e de poucos indicadores — não de mais detalhe operacional.

items.q: The phrase "from a cost centre to a source of strategic capability" suggests that…
options: cost per unit is the only metric that matters
the board should manage logistics directly
logistics is usually seen as merely an expense to be minimised
items.why: Inferência: a mudança de percepção implica que, por padrão, a logística é vista só como custo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentando a nova seção de logística do board pack. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, before you turn the page, let me explain what I have changed. The logistics section used to be that weekly operations dashboard — thirty-odd metrics, dwell times, pick rates, a wall of red and green. Useful for my team on a Monday morning. Almost useless to this board.

I have replaced it with six indicators. Service level trend by quarter, so you see direction rather than a single week. Cost per unit over time. Concentration of volume — and this is the one I want you to sit with, because seventy per cent of our outbound now runs through a single carrier in a single region. That is a capability question, not a cost question.

There is also an honest read of exceptions: what went wrong last quarter and how we resolved it. And a simple risk rating against the two scenarios that would actually hurt us.

What I am not giving you is the detail. If a shipment is late this week, that is my job, not yours. Your job is to decide whether logistics can carry the strategy for the next three years — and these six numbers are enough to have that conversation properly.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did the logistics section of the board pack used to be?
options: A risk rating against future scenarios
The weekly operations dashboard with around thirty metrics
A written narrative with no numbers
items.why: "that weekly operations dashboard — thirty-odd metrics… a wall of red and green."

items.q: Which indicator does Harry specifically ask the board to sit with?
options: The service level trend by quarter
items.why: "Concentration of volume — and this is the one I want you to sit with."

items.q: Why does Harry frame the carrier concentration as "a capability question, not a cost question"?
options: Because the board sets carrier prices
Because the carrier is cheaper than the alternatives
Because reliance on one carrier and region is a strategic risk, not just an expense
Because concentration lowers cost per unit
items.why: Inferência: 70% do outbound num só transportador e região é uma vulnerabilidade estratégica, além do custo.

items.q: What does Harry mean when he says a late shipment "is my job, not yours"?
options: The board should approve every shipment
The board is responsible for daily delivery
Operational detail belongs to management, while the board decides strategy
items.why: Inferência: ele separa o operacional (dele) da decisão estratégica (do board).

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's overall message to the board?
options: Confident that fewer, translated indicators serve the board better
Uncertain about which metrics to include
Defensive and reluctant to share bad news
Focused mainly on cutting logistics costs
items.why: Inferência: ele defende com convicção a troca de trinta métricas por seis indicadores relevantes ao board.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The board wants direction, not a snapshot." Here direction means…
options: the way a metric is trending over time
items.why: Direction, no contexto de KPIs, é a tendência — para onde o número está indo ao longo do tempo.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Running seventy per cent of outbound through one carrier is a dangerous ___ of volume."
items.why: Concentration = concentração: acúmulo de volume num único ponto, um risco.

items.q: Risk rating on a board pack is best described as…
options: a simple assessment of exposure to the biggest known scenarios
a detailed audit of every shipment
the credit score of a carrier
items.why: Risk rating = avaliação de risco: leitura simples da exposição aos cenários mais relevantes.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "An honest read of ___ shows what went wrong and how it was resolved."
items.why: Exception = exceção: o que fugiu do padrão e como foi tratado.

items.q: "Logistics should be seen as a source of capability, not just a cost centre." A cost centre is…
options: a part of the business viewed only as an expense to control
items.why: Cost centre = centro de custo: área vista apenas como despesa, não como geradora de valor.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de board sobre KPIs. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The directors need to sign off on the new dashboard." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the board pack format across every function next quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "A single carrier trend will not move the needle for the board." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Let me walk you through the six indicators." To walk someone through something is to…
items.why: Walk through = explicar passo a passo, conduzir pela lógica.

items.q: "Don't lose sight of the carrier concentration risk." This means don't…
options: forget or stop paying attention to it
items.why: Lose sight of = perder de vista, deixar de dar atenção a algo importante.
